name: The Umoja wa Akina Mama Absent Treasurer
venue: Mama Salome's Sitting Room, South B, Nairobi
description: The treasurer of the Umoja wa Akina Mama chama failed to attend the April 2009 monthly meeting, taking the contribution envelope from the previous month with her. She sent a text message at 2:14 PM reading 'I am coming.' She did not come. The envelope's contents have never been confirmed. She remains treasurer.
prose: The Umoja wa Akina Mama chama held its April 2009 monthly meeting at the sitting room of Mama Salome Atieno, South B, Nairobi, as had been the rotation for that quarter. Eleven of the twelve members were present by 2:00 PM. The absent member was Mrs. Gladys Muthoni Kariuki, the chama's treasurer, who had held the position since the group's founding in 2004 and who was in custody of the contribution envelope from the March meeting, which had not yet been banked.

At 2:14 PM, Mrs. Kariuki sent a text message to the group chairlady, Mama Salome, reading: 'I am coming.' The meeting proceeded with the social agenda. At 3:30 PM a second message arrived: 'Almost there.' At 4:45 PM, as members were beginning to gather their handbags, a third message arrived: 'Something came up. I will explain on Saturday.' No further messages were sent that day. Mrs. Kariuki did not attend the Saturday meeting either, citing a family matter in Nyeri.

The March contribution envelope — containing the pooled contributions of all twelve members, estimated at between Ksh 24,000 and Ksh 36,000 depending on which member's recollection is used — was presented by Mrs. Kariuki at the May meeting. She did not offer an accounting of the intervening five weeks. The chairlady did not request one, in the interest of group harmony. Two members have stated privately that the envelope felt lighter than expected.

Mrs. Kariuki remains the chama's treasurer as of the most recent update to this record. No audit has been conducted. The incident is designated OPEN on the basis that the contents of the March envelope have never been independently verified.
heritageTrustNote: The Heritage Trust notes that the phrase 'in the interest of group harmony' appears in four separate oral history testimonies relating to this incident, always offered as a reason for not pursuing a line of inquiry. The Trust has preserved all four uses without comment.

pullQuote.quote: She said 'almost there' at half past three. We were in South B. There is nowhere that is almost there for two hours.
pullQuote.attribution: Mrs. Beatrice Njoki, 58, Chama member since founding
